questions.question: What should you do to control your motorcycle properly while turning?

options.text: Speed up before entering the turn.
Look ahead through the turn to see what is coming.
Stop completely before entering the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead through the turn to see what is coming.
questions.explanation: To control your motorcycle through a turn, look ahead through the turn by turning only your head. Slow down before the turn and lean your motorcycle in the direction you are turning.

questions.question: What should a motorcycle rider tell their passenger to do?

options.text: Sit as far back as possible.
Put their feet on the muffler.
Get on the motorcycle after the engine is started.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get on the motorcycle after the engine is started.
questions.explanation: Give your passenger complete safety instructions before you leave. Have them get on the motorcycle only after you start the engine. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding you and hold onto your waist, hips, or belt firmly. They should keep both feet on the footrests at all times, even when stopped.

questions.question: Drivers entering the highway from a ramp on your right may not see your motorcycle. What should you do?

options.text: Move to the left side of your lane so they can share it if needed.
Move to another lane if necessary.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to another lane if necessary.
questions.explanation: Give plenty of space to vehicles entering the highway from a ramp. Move to a lane farther from the ramp if you can. If you cannot change lanes, slow down to give the vehicle room to enter safely.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes?

options.text: Signal, check your mirrors, and turn your head.
Turn your head and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, and turn your head.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to see if the path is clear before you change lanes.

questions.question: What is true about brightly-colored helmets?

options.text: They may help other drivers see you.
They do not improve how visible you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may help other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: A brightly-colored helmet is a good choice. It protects your head in a crash and helps other road users see you.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to stop the wobble.
Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly release the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly release the throttle.
questions.explanation: Speeding up will make the wobble worse and is dangerous. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly without fighting the wobble, slowly reduce your speed, and lean forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as you can.

questions.question: How do you lean a motorcycle when turning?

options.text: Press the handgrip opposite the direction of the turn.
Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle must lean to turn. Press on the handgrip in the direction you want to turn to make the motorcycle lean that way.

questions.question: What should you NOT check on your tires before riding?
questions.correctAnswerText: Flexibility.
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tire air pressure, tread, and general wear. You do not need to check flexibility.

questions.question: What is true about approved helmets?

options.text: They let you see clearly to the sides.
You do not have to wear one if you think it limits your view.

questions.correctAnswerText: They let you see clearly to the sides.
questions.explanation: Some riders worry that helmets limit their vision, but this is not true. Approved helmets allow you to see as far to the sides as you need for safe riding.

questions.question: What is a major effect of drinking alcohol?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slows down body functions.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows down your physical and mental abilities.

questions.question: When you stop your motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Use both brakes at the same time.
Use only the front or rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes together whenever you slow down or stop.

questions.question: When does a helmet NOT give the best protection?

options.text: When it is certified by the DOT.
When it is free of damage.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it has cracks.
questions.explanation: A good helmet must have DOT approval, fit snugly, and have no defects like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: Your body gets rid of one drink per hour. If someone drinks 7 drinks in 3 hours, how many drinks are still in their system 3 hours later?
questions.correctAnswerText: Four
questions.explanation: Subtract the hours since their last drink from the total drinks consumed. Seven drinks consumed, minus six hours that have passed, equals four drinks remaining.

questions.question: What helps other drivers see you at an intersection?

options.text: Make eye contact with other drivers.
Ride close to the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlight on.
questions.explanation: Always ride with your headlight on whenever your motorcycle is running. This is the best way to help others see you.

questions.question: What should you do when riding near stopped or slow cars?

options.text: Pull over and wait for traffic to move.
Ride on the shoulder to pass quickly.
Weave between cars to pass quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not weave between cars.
questions.explanation: Weaving between cars is dangerous. You could hit an opening door or a car pulling into traffic. You also have no room to escape if something goes wrong. Never ride on the shoulder.

questions.question: Before riding, check everything about your tires except:

options.text: How much air is in them.
The condition of the tire sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: How shiny they are.
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tire pressure, tread wear, and the condition of the sidewalls and tread.

questions.question: What is the main active ingredient in marijuana?
questions.correctAnswerText: THC
questions.explanation: The main active ingredient in marijuana is called tetrahydrocannabinol, or THC.

questions.question: When a vehicle passes you from behind, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: In the center of the lane.
On the left side of the lane.
On the right side of the lane.
It does not matter which part of the lane you use.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. This keeps you away from the passing vehicle and reduces the risk of a collision.

questions.question: What should you do if another vehicle is following you too closely?

options.text: Let the other driver pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the other driver pass you.
questions.explanation: The safest way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass. Change lanes safely and allow them to go ahead. Speeding up will only make things more dangerous.
